name: Data Cleaning & Transform
description: Load messy data, handle missing values, transform columns, and produce a clean dataset.

cells.code:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Generate messy sample data (simulating a real-world CSV import)
np.random.seed(99)
n = 200

df = pd.DataFrame({
    'customer_id': range(1, n+1),
    'name': [f'Customer {i}' if np.random.random() > 0.05 else None for i in range(1, n+1)],
    'email': [f'user{i}@example.com' if np.random.random() > 0.1 else 'INVALID' for i in range(1, n+1)],
    'age': [np.random.randint(18, 80) if np.random.random() > 0.08 else None for _ in range(n)],
    'signup_date': pd.date_range('2023-01-01', periods=n, freq='2D').astype(str),
    'revenue': [round(np.random.exponential(150), 2) if np.random.random() > 0.12 else None for _ in range(n)],
    'country': np.random.choice(['US', 'UK', 'DE', 'FR', 'JP', 'AU', None], n),
})

print(f"Raw dataset: {df.shape[0]} rows, {df.shape[1]} columns")
print(f"\nMissing values:")
print(df.isnull().sum())
df.head()

# Step 1: Handle missing values
df_clean = df.copy()

# Fill missing names
df_clean['name'] = df_clean['name'].fillna('Unknown')

# Fill missing ages with median
df_clean['age'] = df_clean['age'].fillna(df_clean['age'].median())

# Fill missing revenue with 0 (no purchase)
df_clean['revenue'] = df_clean['revenue'].fillna(0)

# Fill missing country
df_clean['country'] = df_clean['country'].fillna('Unknown')

print("After filling missing values:")
print(df_clean.isnull().sum())

# Step 2: Fix data types and invalid values

# Fix invalid emails
df_clean['email_valid'] = df_clean['email'].str.contains('@') & (df_clean['email'] != 'INVALID')
df_clean.loc[df_clean['email'] == 'INVALID', 'email'] = None

# Convert signup_date to datetime
df_clean['signup_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df_clean['signup_date'])

# Add derived columns
df_clean['signup_year'] = df_clean['signup_date'].dt.year
df_clean['signup_month'] = df_clean['signup_date'].dt.month
df_clean['age_group'] = pd.cut(df_clean['age'], bins=[0, 25, 35, 50, 65, 100], labels=['18-25', '26-35', '36-50', '51-65', '65+'])

print(f"Clean dataset: {df_clean.shape[0]} rows, {df_clean.shape[1]} columns")
df_clean.dtypes

# Step 3: Aggregate and summarize
summary = df_clean.groupby('country').agg(
    customers=('customer_id', 'count'),
    avg_revenue=('revenue', 'mean'),
    total_revenue=('revenue', 'sum'),
    avg_age=('age', 'mean'),
    valid_emails=('email_valid', 'sum')
).round(2).sort_values('total_revenue', ascending=False)

summary

# Step 4: Visualize the clean data
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))

# Revenue distribution
axes[0].hist(df_clean[df_clean['revenue'] > 0]['revenue'], bins=30, color='#89b4fa', alpha=0.8)
axes[0].set_title('Revenue Distribution (non-zero)', color='white')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Revenue ($)', color='#a6adc8')
axes[0].tick_params(colors='#a6adc8')

# Customers by country
country_counts = df_clean['country'].value_counts()
axes[1].barh(country_counts.index, country_counts.values, color='#a6e3a1')
axes[1].set_title('Customers by Country', color='white')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Count', color='#a6adc8')
axes[1].tick_params(colors='#a6adc8')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
